items.claim: Client-supplied x-vercel-isr header reopens the x_astro_path override bypass in every function, including _render
items.consequence: If a client can send `x-vercel-isr: 1` and have it reach the function, the path-override bypass that #15959 closed is back: `GET /api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private` with that header renders `/api/private`. That skips Vercel routing, edge middleware, and firewall rules scoped to the real path, and ISR can cache the result under the attacker's `x_astro_path` key. The check lives in the shared entrypoint, so the non-ISR `_render` function honors it too, even though Vercel never invokes `_render` as ISR. That covers deployments with no ISR configured and ISR-excluded routes that go through middleware. Running the built fixture confirmed it: `_render` returned `{"id":"private"}` for `/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private` with the header, and `{"id":"public"}` without it. Whether Vercel's edge strips a client-supplied `x-vercel-isr` could not be checked offline, so exploitability is still unconfirmed.
items.proposed_fix: Gate the ISR branch on something a client cannot set on _render: bake a build-time flag into the _isr function only (e.g. an `isr` field on `virtual:astro-vercel:config` set from buildISRFolder, or a separate ISR entry) and also require `url.pathname === '/_isr'` alongside `request.headers.get('x-vercel-isr') === '1'` (assumes Vercel invokes the ISR function at /_isr, per ISR_PATH in index.ts:63). Confirm with Vercel docs/support whether the edge strips or overwrites a client-supplied `x-vercel-isr`; if it does not, ISR invocations need a platform-injected secret instead. Add a case to test/path-override-security.test.js: _render.fetch(new Request('https://example.com/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private', { headers: { 'x-vercel-isr': '1' } })) must return id 'public' (this fails against the current code).

items.claim: ISR path-rewrite fix ships with no handler-level regression test
items.consequence:
#15959 caused every ISR route to 404, and it shipped because isr.test.js only checks the generated prerender-config and routes, never the handler's behavior. This PR fixes the handler but adds no test (the PR body says so), so the same 404 regression could come back unnoticed. It is cheap to test in-process: the built isr fixture's `_isr` handler returns 404 for `/_isr?x_astro_path=/one` without the header and 200 `

One

` with `x-vercel-isr: 1`.
items.proposed_fix:
In test/isr.test.js, load _isr.func like loadFunctionModule in path-override-security.test.js and fetch `new Request('https://example.com/_isr?x_astro_path=/one', { headers: { 'x-vercel-isr': '1' } })`, asserting status 200 and that the body contains '

One

'.

native_payload.verdict_reasoning: Open P0 #1 (confirmed by the validator): the new else-if at entrypoint.ts:24 honors x_astro_path for any request that carries x-vercel-isr: 1. Because the entrypoint is shared, _render honors it too, which reopens the path-override bypass #15959 closed. Fix order: #1 first, restricting the override to the _isr function (build-time ISR flag and/or url.pathname === '/_isr') and adding the forged-header _render test to path-override-security.test.js. Before settling on a header gate, confirm whether Vercel strips a client-supplied x-vercel-isr; if it does not, ISR invocations need a platform-injected secret. Then #2, a handler-level _isr test proving ISR still returns 200.
native_payload.intent: Restore ISR rendering in the Vercel adapter. #15959 required the middleware secret for path overrides, so Vercel's /_isr?x_astro_path=<path> invocations 404ed. This PR also honors the x_astro_path query param when the request carries x-vercel-isr: 1, and it must not reopen the untrusted path-override bypass #15959 closed.

triage_groups.title: Gate the ISR path override to the ISR function, then pin both halves with tests
triage_groups.context: Both findings sit on the new else-if branch at entrypoint.ts:24-25: #1 is the untrusted override it reopens on _render, #2 is the missing positive test that ISR still renders.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Handle #1 first (restrict the branch to the _isr function via a build-time flag and/or url.pathname === '/_isr', plus the forged-header _render test), then #2 (an _isr handler test for /_isr?x_astro_path=/one with x-vercel-isr: 1 returning 200).
triage_groups.why: Tightening the gate for #1 is exactly the kind of change that can re-break ISR the way #15959 did; #2's test is what proves it didn't.
triage_groups.kind: apply-queue after #1's platform check (whether Vercel strips client x-vercel-isr decides between a gate and a platform-injected secret)

residual_risks: Platform assumption behind both halves of the fix: ISR only works if Vercel reliably sets `x-vercel-isr: 1` on ISR invocations, and the bypass in #1 is only closed at the platform level if Vercel strips or overwrites a client-supplied value. Neither could be verified offline, and the PR's manual e2e deployment exercises only the positive half (correctness, security, testing, adversarial).

With ISR enabled, a direct request to `/_isr?x_astro_path=<excluded route>` may reach the _isr function (fixture config.json routes begin with `handle: filesystem`); if Vercel sets `x-vercel-isr` on that invocation, routes listed in `isr.exclude` would be rendered by the ISR function, cached per x_astro_path, and, with middlewareMode 'edge', rendered without the edge middleware that normally fronts them (index.ts:476-490 routes excluded paths to MIDDLEWARE_PATH/NODE_PATH). A pathname-only `/_isr` guard for #1 does not close this; rejecting override targets that are not ISR routes would. Platform-dependent and unconfirmed offline (adversarial P2 at anchor 50, routed here; also raised by correctness and security residual risks).
